Name: Establishing a Legionnaires’ disease hotline.
Title: A Local Law to amend the administrative code of the city of New York, in relation to establishing a Legionnaires’ disease hotline

History.Description: This Introduction was Introduced by Council
This Introduction was Referred to Comm by Council to the Committee on Health

Summary: This bill would require that the Department of Health and Mental Hygiene (DOHMH) establish and maintain a hotline for the public to request information about Legionnaires’ disease and disease outbreaks in NYC, as well as to provide hotline users with referrals to resources and medical services.
Text:
Be it enacted by the Council as follows:
      
      
      Section 1. Chapter 1 of title 17 of the administrative code of the city of New York is amended by adding a new section 17-194.2 to read as follows:
      � 17-194.2 Legionnaires' disease hotline. a. Definitions. For the purposes of this section, the term "healthcare provider" means an individual duly licensed or otherwise authorized to practice a health profession pursuant to applicable law, such as a physician, registered professional nurse, nurse practitioner, and physician assistant.
      b. Hotline. The commissioner shall establish and maintain a hotline for the public to request information about Legionnaires' disease and disease outbreaks. The commissioner shall make the hotline available during the summer months and when Legionnaires' outbreaks occur. The hotline shall have healthcare providers available to respond to calls when appropriate and shall provide callers with medical and public health information relating to Legionnaire's disease, resources and referrals to medical guidance and care. 
      � 2. This local law takes effect immediately.
